judged_text: The iteration silently changed failure semantics for the pre-existing path: the console.error zodError logging was removed and the code now throws via parseRefreshTokenResponse on schema failure, ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Existing self-hosters who never enable credential sync lose the previous graceful behavior (log and continue with stale-but-usable credentials) and instead get a thrown error on any malformed Microsoft token response — an objective change smuggled into the sync PR without being called out for acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the prior code used `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, only `console.error(...)` while continuing with the existing `o365AuthCredentials` (i.e., effectively keeping stale credentials) and proceeding to `prisma.credential.update(...)`. The new code replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which (per `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on any schema failure regardless of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (the flag only changes which schema is used, not whether it throws). This is a verifiable change to failure semantics for non-sync deployments and can turn previously non-fatal malformed/changed Microsoft token responses into hard failures.
